games.reason: Bloat is the pet peeve here: a huge rulebook and a long runtime that partly disguise kingmaking and swingy politics, though the strong faction asymmetry keeps it from a 2.
The card-hand-as-resource core is a genuinely fresh decision and good play is visibly rewarded, but the bloat and fiddly setup keep it a step below a classic.
Competent engine builder with real route choices, but it is familiar parts, some corporations and cards are dead picks, and the card-draw luck swings results.
A modern classic with elegant rules and a clear shelf pitch, but I will not give it a 5 because of the trade-driven kingmaking and the dice swing.
One fresh, elegant decision in a rulebook that fits on a postcard, easy to pitch in one sentence, and I would defend it in any shop.
Distinctive hook and clear teach, but the core decision is thin and not skill-driven, so it is a fine filler for the right audience.
Thin core hidden behind art and humour with swingy luck and many dead cards; it is a known shape of Russian-roulette-with-a-deck rather than new design.
Elegant, clean rules and a clear audience with a real tension between claiming and blocking routes, only lightly solved by longest-route greed, so polish is all that is left.
